# Introduction
`Github pages` is an optional Github service which publishes pages directly from a Github repository. Using documentation with your repo, it creates a user-friendly website with the key information about your package. [Here](https://molgenis.github.io/ds-tidyverse-client/) is an example from the `dsTidyverseClient` package. Creating a website using Github pages only requires a few steps.

# Create the documentation within the R package
For both the client- and server-side packages, run:
```r
devtools::build_site()
```
In the file `.Rbuildignore`, below the existing entries add the line:
```r
docs
```
Commit and push the changes to your remote repository.

# Set up Github pages in your repository
- Navigate to the home page of your server-side repository, and click `settings/pages`. 
- Under `Build and Deployment/branch`, change 'None' to the name of the branch you want to build the documentation from. In `dsExample` and `dsExampleClient` we are building from the master branch, so we set this to `master`. You can chose to build from a separate branch if you have a different workflow. 
- Change `/root` to `/docs`. Click `save`. 
- Navigate to the homepage of your repository. In the `about` section click the cog (settings button) and check 'Use your GitHub Pages website'. A link to the website will now be shown.

Now repeat for the client-side repository.
